prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: Operating and Financial Metrics (language en).
Grid: 5 columns × 7 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Metric" · longest unbreakable word 82px · one-line width 407px
  col 2: header "FY 2022" · longest unbreakable word 61px · one-line width 61px
  col 3: header "FY 2023" · longest unbreakable word 62px · one-line width 62px
  col 4: header "FY 2024" · longest unbreakable word 58px · one-line width 61px
  col 5: header "Q1 2025" · longest unbreakable word 63px · one-line width 63px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
This table cannot fit without splitting words at 360px. You MAY choose a total wider than 359px (the reader then scrolls horizontally), or squeeze and accept splits — a design decision.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"A compact operating and financial KPI table for comparing six metrics across FY 2022, FY 2023, FY 2024 and Q1 2025; readers use it to scan trends over time rather than read prose.","reading":"Scan the first column down to find the metric, then read across the four period columns to compare values. The metric column is the row index; the four period columns form a matched numeric band. Long metric labels will wrap at word boundaries, and period headers can stack as FY / 2022 and Q1 / 2025, but digits and currency/percent tokens should not split.","groups":["Column 1: row-label/index column, separate from all values.","Columns 2–5: one peer group of period-value columns; equal width is appropriate because they play the same role and support across-row comparison. Q1 2025 is a shorter latest period but still belongs to this band."],"keep_intact":["Metric names' unbreakable words such as 'percentage', 'acquisition' and 'recurring' — no mid-word splits","Numeric values including $, commas, decimals and % (e.g. $1,800, 71.3%)","Year digits 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025 — headers may break only after 'FY' or 'Q1'"],"may_wrap":["Long metric labels at spaces or commas, over 2–4 lines","Period headers into two lines: FY / 2022, Q1 / 2025","Header rows and metric rows may grow taller; numeric body cells should stay on one line"]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r2A: widths [176, 84, 84, 84, 84] · table 513×487px · row heights [36, 83, 36, 106, 60, 83, 83] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 4 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 153px
Design r2B: widths [224, 84, 84, 84, 84] · table 561×394px · row heights [36, 60, 36, 83, 60, 60, 60] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 201px
Design r2C: widths [150, 86, 86, 86, 86] · table 495×557px · row heights [36, 83, 60, 129, 83, 83, 83] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 5 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 135px

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}
